declared.reason: Complete the initial protocol before the first tagged 0.2.0 release. The invalid_plan_output diagnostic now includes the measured saved-file size or an honest read lower bound and the unchanged 8 MiB limit. Its error code, result shape, refusal boundaries, payload handling, and execution behavior are unchanged. No tagged release could have stored or consumed an earlier protocol-1 contract; all development contract counters remain 1.

Expose the existing decoded-result validator for authenticated delivery without changing the runner command, execution checks, result fields, log framing, or acceptance rules. The new function requires an explicit operation and ID and delegates to the same validator used by the existing parser. The receiver and sender are not yet connected to the runner command; protocol version 1 remains unchanged.

Complete the initial durable result transport before the first tagged 0.2.0 release. Explicit TLS delivery validates projected credentials and operation/Pod identity before child dispatch, sends the completed result with bounded retries, and never falls back to logs. Durable Plan results contain the exact validated plaintext bytes instead of process-key ciphertext; termination summaries retain their payload digest and do not claim acknowledgment. Jobs without delivery configuration retain their existing log protocol during integration. No tagged release could have stored or consumed an earlier protocol-1 contract; the development contract counters remain 1.

Complete the initial durable delivery identity before the first tagged 0.2.0 release. The runner now requires the original resource generation as a literal Job-template input and holds its client certificate to that generation as well as the operation and actual Pod identity. A shared Job projection fixes the TLS credential Secret, read-only mount, downward API identity, and absence of Kubernetes credentials; legacy Jobs without durable delivery flags retain their existing behavior. No tagged release could have stored or consumed an earlier protocol-1 contract; development contract counters remain 1.

Complete the initial 0.2.0 result transport before the first tagged release. Durable publication now uses the dedicated immutable PtahResultRecord API instead of workload Secrets, preserving digest reservation, chunk identity checks, completion readback, payload bounds, and TLS redelivery. The storage change grants no Kubernetes API credential to the runner and requires no database Secret reads. The log path and wire payload are unchanged; development protocol counters remain 1.

Complete the initial durable transport before the first tagged 0.2.0 release. Before starting SQL, a configured runner authenticates its projected credential through a bounded mTLS HEAD request with live delivery-authority checks. This request publishes nothing and is neither execution permission nor a durable receipt. Failed authentication or receiver unavailability stops the child; completed results retain identical-byte redelivery. Legacy Jobs without delivery configuration are unchanged. No tagged release consumed an earlier protocol-1 contract; development counters remain 1.

Complete durable publication admission before the first tagged 0.2.0 release. Result records now share strict canonical manifest, metadata, owner, length, and digest checks between admission and readback. Completion validates every persisted chunk UID and the full protocol under the canonical credential and live operation authority. Identical concurrent writes remain idempotent; completed publications cannot be healed by recreating missing members. The wire payload and execution behavior are unchanged. No tagged release consumed an earlier protocol-1 contract; development counters remain 1.

Complete durable result consumption before the first tagged 0.2.0 release. The result store can locate and verify a publication by its immutable attempt without reading the producing Pod or Job. Consumers must check the returned full binding and protocol against the persisted operation. The runner wire payload and execution behavior are unchanged; development protocol counters remain 1.

Complete receiver trust reload before the first tagged 0.2.0 release. Rotating receivers revalidate the current client CA at every authority check, including after upload and before durable completion, so an existing TLS connection cannot retain removed trust. Runner payload, execution checks, and bounded retries are unchanged. No tagged release consumed an earlier protocol-1 contract; development counters remain 1.

Separate immutable credential identity decoding for cleanup from live client authentication. Cleanup can read a retained expired certificate after its canonical record disappears, then check the original resource before deleting its Secret projection. ClientIdentity still rejects expired and not-yet-valid leaves; TLS, live authority, runner payload, execution, and retry behavior are unchanged. No tagged release consumed an earlier protocol-1 contract; development counters remain 1.

Add the immutable retired result-record role and a cleanup-only intent binding reader before the first 0.2.0 tag. Retirement fences new delivery while existing receipts remain readable, and its API creation time starts the recovery window. Runner payloads, TLS identities, and SQL execution limits are unchanged. No tagged release consumed an earlier protocol-1 contract; development counters remain 1.

Add an immutable attempt index to new result publications before the first 0.2.0 tag. Previously persisted unindexed publications remain readable and retryable. Cleanup validates child ownership and permits finalizing foreground deletion without changing payloads, digests, delivery identity, or SQL execution. No tagged release consumed an earlier protocol-1 contract; development counters remain 1.

Complete result redelivery before the first tagged 0.2.0 release. When admission refuses a CREATE of changed result bytes before storage returns AlreadyExists, the store now identifies the immutable content conflict by direct read and the receiver returns the existing HTTP 409 contract instead of a temporary 503. Identical-byte retries, wire encoding, result validation, SQL execution, and all other write errors are unchanged. No tagged release consumed this development transport; protocol counters remain 1.

Complete the initial durable protocol before the first tagged 0.2.0 release. A runner whose protocol differs from its Job now exits with code 2 and the bounded mismatch diagnostic before reading delivery credentials, contacting the receiver, or starting the executor. It does not attempt a receipt under a foreign contract. Legacy framed refusals and compatible durable results are unchanged. No tagged release consumed an earlier protocol-1 contract; development counters remain 1.

Complete bounded receiver preflight retries before the first tagged 0.2.0 release. Temporary receiver or transport failures now retry the read-only authentication request within the existing attempt and total delivery limits. Definitive authority refusals remain immediate; the runner starts its child only after authentication succeeds and never repeats SQL during result redelivery. Wire fields, identities, payload bounds and legacy delivery are unchanged. No tagged release consumed this development transport; protocol counters remain 1.

Add bounded Pod-token transport components before the first tagged 0.2.0 release. Token authentication requires explicit receiver configuration, server TLS validation, a receiver-only audience, and a refreshed token for each request. Existing runner and manager entrypoints still select mTLS; their accepted flags, result payload, execution checks, SQL behavior, and retry bounds are unchanged. The token components are not yet connected to operation Jobs or the installed receiver. No tagged release consumed an earlier protocol-1 contract; development counters remain 1.

Complete receiver-audience Pod-token delivery before the first tagged 0.2.0 release. The installed runner now uses --result-token, verified server TLS, and a token reread on every bounded preflight or delivery attempt. Public template inputs bind the operation and downward API Job/Pod identities; the receiver rechecks TokenReview, immutable first-Pod binding, and live authority. Per-operation Secret creation is removed. Payloads, size limits, SQL execution guards, same-byte retries, and unknown-outcome recovery are unchanged. No tagged release consumed this development transport; protocol counters remain 1.

Preserve bounded, sanitized preflight and result-delivery failure causes in runner diagnostics, including the final HTTP status after retry exhaustion. The wire payload, durable acknowledgment, authorization, retry budget, SQL execution behavior, and no-log-fallback rule are unchanged; protocol version 1 remains compatible.

Complete transient receiver recovery before the first tagged 0.2.0 release. Preflight and identical-byte result delivery now permit up to 120 attempts at one-second intervals instead of exhausting four immediate refusals in three seconds. The existing two-minute total deadline and 30-second request deadline still bound each retry sequence. Definitive authority refusals, wire payloads, durable acknowledgment, SQL execution guards, and the no-reexecution and no-log-fallback rules are unchanged. No tagged release consumed this development transport; protocol counters remain 1.

Allow an identical result-record CREATE when another publisher creates that member and completes between the admission reads. After observing completion, admission re-reads the member and still requires its exact immutable bytes, ownership, live UID, and absence of deletion. Missing or conflicting members remain refused, and API read failures remain errors. This changes a receiver-side admission race in a transitive runner package; wire payloads, durable receipts, live authority checks, SQL execution, retry budgets, and the no-reexecution rule are unchanged. Protocol version 1 remains compatible.

Complete small-result atomic storage in the unreleased 0.2.0 transport. A result up to 256 KiB can commit in its immutable intent; larger and already-started publications retain the chunked format. The paired receiver, runner, and consumer accept the exact root receipt as well as a chunked completion, with unchanged bytes, digest, UID binding, live authorization, retry deadlines, and no SQL replay. Admission validates the complete inline protocol before CREATE. No tagged release consumed this development representation; contract counters remain 1.

Move the post-upload authority check to the publisher before its first write. Atomic results use this as their commit check; chunked results still revalidate after their chunks and before completion or an existing receipt. Request authentication before reading the body, admission authorization, exact durable readback, and identical-byte retries remain required. This removes duplicate live reads without changing wire payloads, identities, execution authority, or protocol version 1.

Reuse an immutable intent already read and verified within the same result publication or load instead of reading it twice. The persisted UID, owner, binding, manifest, digest, size, and chunk-completion checks remain required; a CREATE response does not replace durable readback. This changes the result store in the runner's transitive dependency closure. Wire payloads, receipt formats, live authorization, SQL execution, and retry limits are unchanged. Protocol version 1 remains compatible.

Update golang.org/x/net to v0.60.0 for the October 8 HTTP/2 security fixes. This changes a dependency in the runner source closure. Runner commands, payloads, result validation, delivery identity, SQL authority, and retry limits are unchanged. The security fixes reject malformed HTTP/2 traffic without changing the protocol-1 application contract.

Take the drift categories of the Ptah v0.13.0 executor before the first tagged 0.2.0 release. The closed vocabulary gains the 31 categories that release emits, and a result frame may carry up to 128 summaries so the whole vocabulary fits. A frame naming an unknown category is still refused, which is the refusal an older controller gives a newer runner. No tagged release consumed an earlier protocol-1 contract; development counters remain 1.

Update sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime to v0.25.2 and k8s.io/utils to its October 7 revision (#641). The runner links controller-runtime's client, scheme and metrics packages; v0.25.2 corrects how subresource create options are applied and adds a metric for the experimental read-your-writes client, and neither changes what the runner accepts, enforces or returns. Runner commands, payloads, result validation, delivery identity, SQL authority and retry limits are unchanged.

Authenticate result PUTs before reading their bounded bodies, then check authentication and live operation authority immediately before durable publication and again before chunk completion. Removing the earlier duplicate authority read changes receiver-side API demand, not runner commands, HEAD preflight authorization, payload validation, wire documents, receipts, upload bounds, or retry behavior. Unauthorized publication remains refused at its write boundary; runner protocol 1 is unchanged.

Bound connection establishment by the existing per-attempt timeout so a stalled dial cannot occupy every result-delivery retry. Preflight and result upload keep their overall deadlines, attempt count, payload and receipt formats, authentication, live authority checks, and child-execution boundary. Transport retries do not rerun SQL. This restores the intended retry behavior without changing the protocol-1 contract.

Update oras.land/oras-go/v2 from v2.6.2 to v2.6.4 (#664). The runner links its errdef, content and registry packages and three internal ones to parse references, and all six are byte-identical between the two versions; the fixes are in the file and OCI stores, the remote auth client and the retry policy, which the runner does not link. The digest moved because go.sum did. Runner commands, payloads, result validation, delivery identity, SQL authority and retry limits are unchanged.

Take Ptah v0.14.0's documents (#678). A migration run report may carry Ptah's failure object, the failed statement's position and the database's SQLSTATE and error number with no text; the runner holds it to the run, carries it in the result frame, and refuses a document it contradicts. The drift vocabulary takes v0.14.0's categories: feature_changes and feature_access_<effect>, bare or with a kind, and undecided, and 31 per-object categories leave it. A report naming more categories than a frame holds is refused before framing. Schema plan and apply reports are read at their contract version 2, whose changes touch no field the runner reads. An older controller ignores the failure object and refuses a frame naming a category it does not know. The executor image changes in the same release, which retires every plan and approval made under the old one. Commands, payloads, delivery identity, SQL authority and retry limits are unchanged.

Read the plan statements Ptah v0.14.0 writes for a feature owner (#695). A statement that Ptah's extension or row-security policy owner rendered carries transactions, owned, access and access_reason, and the strict plan decoder refused every such plan, so a schema declaring a PostgreSQL extension or a policy could not plan or apply. The four fields are declared and nothing reads them: the plan bytes are carried as before, Ptah folds the access assessment into the severity and refuses a plan that understates it in the dry run the plan Job runs, and the privilege kinds are still read from the SQL. Any other unknown field is still refused. Commands, payloads, result frames, delivery identity, SQL authority and retry limits are unchanged.

Copy a ConfigMap source's snapshot (#698). A new mode, --materialize-source-snapshot with --materialize-to and --content-digest, runs in an init container: it reads the mounted snapshot, refuses it unless the manifest gives the bound content digest, every file has the size and SHA-256 its line names, the manifest is canonical and no other key is present, and only then copies the files into the source volume. It opens no connection and reads no credential. Nothing a plan or an approval made under protocol 1 relies on changed: the operation modes, their commands, payloads, result frames, delivery identity, SQL authority and retry limits are as they were, and an OCI source is fetched as before. A runner without the mode refuses the unknown flag before the container that holds the database URL starts.

Resolve and fetch a Git source (#699). A Resolve operation given a Git source runs Ptah's git pull and returns the commit and the content digest in two new result fields, resolvedCommit and resolvedContentDigest, which the parser admits only on a Resolve and never beside OCI descriptor evidence; a new mode, --fetch-git-source, runs in an init container, pulls the bound commit held to its digest, reads the written files back and copies them only if they give it. Both refuse a credential its Secret does not grant for the URL's host, or trust files whose digests it does not grant, before Ptah runs, with invalid_git_access as a pre-child refusal. Nothing a plan or an approval made under protocol 1 relies on changed: OCI and ConfigMap operations, their commands, payloads, result frames, delivery identity, SQL authority and retry limits are as they were. An older manager ignores the two fields and never sends a Git source.

Read Ptah v0.15.0's schema apply document. Ptah moved `schema apply --json` to contract version 3, which lists the planned operations as units, each with its SQL or a native operation's summary, in place of version 2's statements. The runner now reads version 3 and compares the SQL of each unit with the reviewed plan's statements when it validates a plan, and refuses a unit with no SQL as it refuses any other mismatch. Outcome, plan digest and refusal mean what they meant. Nothing a plan or an approval made under protocol 1 relies on changed: the operation modes, their commands, payloads, result frames, delivery identity, SQL authority and retry limits are as they were. The executor is a bound component, so a plan made under Ptah v0.14.0 is not applied under v0.15.0.

Name why a Git pull failed (#699). When Ptah's git pull exits non-zero at a Resolve or in the fetch container, the runner's error message, and the fetch container's termination message, now end with the last line Ptah wrote to standard error, redacted as the main run's output is and bounded to 512 bytes: a submodule or a Git LFS pointer at the selected path, a host key the known hosts do not pin, a commit the server no longer has. The error code, child_exit at a Resolve and git_source_refused in the fetch, is unchanged. Nothing a plan or an approval made under protocol 1 relies on changed: the operation modes, their commands, payloads, result frames, delivery identity, SQL authority and retry limits are as they were.

Document when a Git source pinned to a commit is refused (#699). Only the doc comment on the API's ref.commit field changed: it now says that Ptah asks the server for the commit by its id, that unless a branch or tag points at the commit it asks only a server that says it gives commits by id, so on any other Resolve refuses the commit once its branch moves on, and that a tag holds one commit on every server. The CRDs carry no descriptions, and the runner's code, its modes, commands, payloads, result frames, delivery identity, SQL authority and retry limits are as they were.

Name a plan the API server refuses to store (#711). The API gains the condition reason PlanPublicationRefused, which the manager sets when it retries a Plan whose plan an admission policy or webhook, a quota, RBAC or the object's size refused. The runner neither sets nor reads condition reasons; its modes, commands, payloads, result frames, delivery identity, SQL authority and retry limits are as they were.

Report how much a Git source's selected files hold (#700). A Git resolution also returns resolvedContentBytes, the sum of the file sizes Ptah's pull reported, which a source policy may bound; the parser refuses it beside no Git resolution and refuses a negative value. The API gains sourcePolicyFrom, which the runner does not read. Nothing else changed: commands, payloads, the OCI and ConfigMap paths, delivery identity, SQL authority and retry limits are as they were, and an older manager ignores the field.

Name a Git commit beside a ConfigMap where the API's doc comments describe plan contract version 2. Only comments in api/v1alpha1 changed; the runner's modes, commands, payloads, result frames, delivery identity, SQL authority and retry limits are as they were.

Name the Git source where the API's doc comments list a schema's and a migration's sources, and where they say verificationPolicyFrom is refused beside it. Only comments in api/v1alpha1 changed; the runner's modes, commands, payloads, result frames, delivery identity, SQL authority and retry limits are as they were.

Keep a bounded journal of lifecycle events in each resource's status (#725). The API gains status.journal on PtahSchema and PtahMigration and status.lastRun.failure on PtahMigration, which the manager writes from transitions it already records. The runner neither reads nor writes either; its modes, commands, payloads, result frames, delivery identity, SQL authority and retry limits are as they were.

Read the database on request (#728). The API gains the operator.ptah.run/read-requested-at annotation and status.lastReadRequest on PtahSchema and PtahMigration, which only the manager reads and writes to bring the next interval read forward. The runner neither reads nor writes either; its modes, commands, payloads, result frames, delivery identity, SQL authority and retry limits are as they were.

Publish the newest revision rows with their time and duration (#726). The migration status document's records gain applied_at and execution_time_ms, which Ptah reports for a row that exists; the history and Apply result frames carry them where the runner dropped them before, and the parser refuses a time on a migration with no row, a duration with no time, a negative duration, and a description or checksum past its bound. An older manager ignores the two fields, and a frame without them reads as before. Commands, payloads, delivery identity, SQL authority and retry limits are as they were.

Run Ptah v0.16.0 and publish the object inventory of the last observation (#727). The closed drift vocabulary gains the 22 categories v0.16.0 adds for the objects it now compares, among them grants, sequences, triggers and views; none leaves it, and a frame naming an unknown category is still refused, as an older controller refuses a newer runner. The drift report gains inventory, a count per kind of object on each side, held to kinds the vocabulary pairs, each once, never negative; an Observe frame carries it as driftInventory in kind order, other frames carry none, and an older manager ignores it. v0.16.0's plan, apply, drift and migration documents decode as v0.15.0's did. The executor image changes, which retires every plan and approval made under the old one. Commands, payloads, delivery identity, SQL authority and retry limits are unchanged.
